question: Can an evidence-compiled soft LoRA subspace retain cross-regime sharing while reducing edit-only interference?
positioning: DSN-inspired shared/private adaptation with SMoRA-related rank-wise activation, distinguished by symbolic molecular-program composition and gradient-evidence routing

data.source: the task-aligned MolProgram corpus with all ten editing benchmark tasks
data.editing: 384 examples for each of the ten frozen tasks (3840 total)
data.gates: byte-identical 120-request de novo and 500-request editing Raw@1 gates from the frozen scale comparison
data.coverage_gate: every mode-property node present in evaluation must have at least 64 training examples

method.shared_initialization: both arms continue from the same 16-step dense warm-up adapter
method.gradient_signature: per-layer per-rank derivative with respect to rank-component scaling, averaged over four examples per mode-property node
method.transfer_graph: signed cosine similarity among normalized gradient signatures
method.compiler: top four signed spectral factors mapped to four positive/negative residual-rank pairs
method.program_composition: elementwise maximum over the mode-property nodes named by the request
method.normalization: each request mask has squared L2 norm 16

control: byte-identical data, initialization, optimizer settings, and rank-16 parameter count with all ranks active

evaluation.primary: Edit-only-5 strict success at source similarity 0.65

reporting: pilot only; report every endpoint and do not promote a confirmatory claim
